key_insight: Latent Drift forecasts slow disease progression by modeling anatomical change in a compressed latent space instead of trying to regenerate full MRI anatomy directly.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this could help anticipate neurodegenerative change earlier and support more personalized monitoring and clinical trial planning.
method: Learns progression as latent drift rather than pixel-level image synthesis.
Uses finite scalar quantization to filter small nuisance fluctuations while keeping consistent structural change.
Designed to avoid identity collapse and the continuous interpolation trap seen in standard generative sequence models.
evidence_signal: In longitudinal 3D brain MRI experiments, the method outperformed diffusion and autoregressive transformer baselines on generative fidelity and clinically relevant metrics.
watch_item: Performance is shown on longitudinal MRI benchmarks, so broader clinical use will depend on external validation and careful handling of scan variability across sites and protocols.
paper_title: Progression as Latent Drift: Generative Forecasting of Slow-Evolving Pathologies
